title: Investigation surface patterns and compact trace notes
content:
Executive summary:
This note captures lightweight patterns for investigation surfaces (what to show first to an operator) and compact trace breadcrumbs we can instrument into our runtime to accelerate triage for tokenized inference. Goal: reduce mean-time-to-insight for latency/cost/quality incidents while keeping trace and query budgets bounded.

Why this doc (context):
- Observability team has many full-length runbooks; operators still spend time stitching traces + dashboard queries for common inference failure modes.
- We want a minimal, reproducible surface that answers the 6 core triage questions in under 90s for high-priority incidents:
  1) Is this service-level or tenant-specific?
  2) Did model selection/routing change recently?
  3) Where is latency accumulating (client, network, runtime token path, postproc)?
  4) Are KV-cache or prefix warms degraded?
  5) Any recent quantization/variant rollouts?
  6) Is token cost abnormal relative to expected token distribution?

Compact metric definitions (primary minimal set):
- ttfb_ms_percentile_95: "time_to_first_byte_ms p95 per route/model" (derive from server span start->first_response).
- token_emit_rate_rps: "tokens emitted per second aggregated by model_version" (used for cost and throughput heatmapping).
- kv_hit_ratio_window_5m: "kv reads satisfied / kv reads windowed 5m" (per-tenant + global).
- session_tail_latency_ms_p99: "latency for last-token emission p99 per session length bin (short/med/long)".
- route_fanout_ratio: "requests that fanout to N>1 models / total requests" (detects multi-model explosion).
- model_fallback_rate: "fallback to cheaper/compatible model variants (per-route)".
- trace_sampling_overhead_pct: "percent extra latency introduced by logging/sampling hooks" (probe metric for our instrumentation).

Tracing breadcrumb schema (compact, small fields):
- trace labels (short):
  - svc: {string} (low-cardinality service alias)
  - route: {string} (API route name)
  - model_v: {string} (short model id/version)
  - tenant: {string:hashed} (hashed tenant id, privacy-safe)
  - kv_warm: {Y|N} (bool string)
  - batch_sz: {int} (batch size)
  - path_cost: {low|med|high} (heuristic token-cost bucket)
- span anchors to emit when possible:
  - span.runtime_infer.start -> runtime_infer.end (include kv_hits, kv_reads, kv_latency_ms)
  - span.kv.prefetch (if prefetch triggered)
  - span.model.load_variant (if model swap occurred)
  - span.routing.decision (policy id, fallback flag)

Dashboard micro-lenses (operator surfaces):
- Incident header widget (single line): incident id, top-1 affected route, p95 delta, total affected tenants.
- Top heatmap: route x model_v; color = p95 latency change vs baseline (last 24h).
- Breadcrumb trace sample row: show 5 most recent sampled traces with compact labels (svc, route, model_v, kv_warm, batch_sz, path_cost) and deep-link to trace explorer.
- Quick-slices: short/medium/long session buckets, with p50/p95/p99 and kv_hit_ratio.
- Cost anomaly mini-panel: token_emit_rate_rps * emit_token_price (approx) with outlier marking by z-score.

Investigation flow (90s first-pass):
1) Open Incident header (widget) -> identify top route and whether multi-tenant.
2) Check route_fanout_ratio and model_fallback_rate -> if high, suspect rollout/routing policy.
3) Pull Breadcrumb trace sample row -> scan for kv_warm and batch_sz patterns.
4) If kv_hit_ratio_window_5m low, open kv-prefetch span and check eviction counters.
5) If path_cost==high across samples, correlate to token_emit_rate changes and new prompt templates (ask product/CS).
6) Decide next action: open rollout rollback, add canary throttle, or escalate to infra.

Sampling & cost heuristics (practical):
- Adaptive priority sampling: sample all traces where path_cost==high or kv_warm==N; sample 1% baseline otherwise.
- Sampling budget per hour per region: cap at 5k full traces/h; prefer compact breadcrumbs for all others.
- Emit compact breadcrumbs always (cheap labels + summary metrics) and full spans only when sampled.

Instrument changes proposed (engineering checklist):
- [ ] Add kv_hit_ratio_window_5m to realtime metrics export (push to metrics bus).
- [ ] Add compact breadcrumb fields to runtime trace header (3 bytes approx per request).
- [ ] Implement adaptive priority sampler plugin in trace pipeline (rules: high path_cost OR kv_warm==N OR fallback==true -> keep).
- [ ] Dashboard micro-lenses: wire the breadcrumb row to trace explorer URL template.
- [ ] Add backlog job to map route -> likely prompt size distribution (to help path_cost mapping).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How do we define path_cost automatically for new models? Quick heuristic: average token length * native model token_factor; follow up with model-performance team.
- Privacy: hashed tenant id is OK for investigator, but do we want tenant alias in private deployments? (ask security).
- Query budget: are 5k full traces/h realistic in worst-case bursts? Need region capacity numbers from SRE.

Short vignettes (examples):
- Vignette A: Large enterprise route sees p95 jump; breadcrumb rows show kv_warm=N across samples -> root cause: tuning TTL expired after cache purge during deploy. Action: roll back TTL change + rewarm probes.
- Vignette B: Multi-model fanout spiking -> route_fanout_ratio indicates a new policy; traces show routing.decision span with policy=policy-x -> quick revert of policy rollout.

Small-scale experiments to run (next 2 weeks):
- Experiment 1: Turn on breadcrumb emission for 20% traffic for three high-volume routes; measure trace_sampling_overhead_pct and query cost.
- Experiment 2: Adaptive sampler rule enabling for a week for canary region; compare incident MTTR to control region.

Notes-to-self / TODOs:
- Reach out to SRE for conservative sampling caps (assign INF-4321).
- Draft privacy proposal for hashed tenant id (Sofia).
- Link this doc into the incident playbook page and create an ops quickcard.

Appendix: useful queries / quick SQL-like psuedocode
- kv_hit_ratio_window_5m(sample): SELECT sum(kv_hits)/sum(kv_reads) FROM metrics WHERE route=R AND ts > now()-5m GROUP BY route;
- top-breadcrumbs: SELECT trace_id, svc, route, model_v, kv_warm, batch_sz, path_cost FROM breadcrumb_table WHERE route=R ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 5;

End.
